title: Valid palindrome
prompt:
PageTurn has a word game: students type a phrase and the app says whether it is a palindrome (reads the same forwards and backwards). Only letters and digits count, and case doesn't matter, so spaces and punctuation are skipped.

Write isPalindrome(text) that returns true or false. Use O(1) extra space: don't build a cleaned or reversed copy of the string.

Examples:

  • isPalindrome("Race car") → true (it is "racecar")
  • isPalindrome("A man, a plan, a canal: Panama") → true
  • isPalindrome("reading") → false
  • isPalindrome("") → true (nothing to contradict it)

Constraints: 0 ≤ text.length ≤ 105, plain ASCII. A character counts if /[a-z0-9]/i.test(ch) is true.

tests.name: simple palindrome with a space and mixed case
punctuation and spaces are ignored
tests.code:
assertEqual(isPalindrome('A man, a plan, a canal: Panama'), true);
assertEqual(isPalindrome('No lemon, no melon!'), true);

tests.name: empty string and single character are palindromes
a string with only punctuation is a palindrome
digits count and are not equal to letters
mismatch near the middle is caught
tests.code:
assertEqual(isPalindrome('abcxba'), false);
assertEqual(isPalindrome('ab_a'), true, 'underscore is not a letter or digit');

hints: "Reads the same forwards and backwards" means: compare the first character with the last, the second with the second-to-last, and so on. That is two pointers from opposite ends.

Start left = 0 and right = text.length - 1. While left < right: if the left character doesn't count, move left right and try again; same for right. Otherwise compare lowercase versions; a mismatch means false.

Shape:

while (left < right) {
  if (!counts(text[left])) { left++; continue; }
  if (!counts(text[right])) { right--; continue; }
  if (text[left].toLowerCase() !== text[right].toLowerCase()) return false;
  left++; right--;
}
return true;
explain:
Time O(n), extra space O(1). Each step moves at least one pointer inward, so there are at most n steps, and you only store two indexes. The "clean, reverse, compare" version is also O(n) time but allocates two extra strings of length n.

In an interview: "Palindrome means mirrored, so I'll compare from both ends with two pointers, skipping non-alphanumeric characters. That's O(n) time and O(1) extra space, versus O(n) space if I built a reversed copy."
